paragraphs: Warrington Borough Council recruits foster carers through Foster4, a joint recruitment hub for councils across Cheshire and Merseyside that Warrington hosts. In May 2024 Foster4 covered eight councils, including Warrington, Halton, Cheshire East, Cheshire West and Chester, Knowsley, Liverpool, St Helens and Wirral, and all eight take part in the Mockingbird model of peer support. The independent agencies listed on this page also look after Warrington children.

The council says more than 350 children and young people in Warrington need a safe and stable foster family. It looks for carers for permanent, short-term and emergency fostering, respite, parent and child placements and short breaks for disabled children.

Its fostering page says mainstream carers receive a skills payment of between £150 and £500 a week, depending on their category, on top of a weekly allowance for each child of between £170 and £258, depending on age. The page does not say which year these rates apply to, so ask Foster4 for the current figures.

Support includes therapeutic visits for newly approved carers during their first year with a child, mentoring by experienced carers, a carer-run foster carer association, a group for carers' own children, a carers' forum and drop-in, and 24-hour support. You can start by requesting an information pack from Foster4, and it is worth comparing what two or three of the agencies below offer too.

sources.title: Foster4 launches in a bid to urgently recruit foster carers (Silk 106.9, May 2024)
